The temporary path uses only the source stem and process ID, and std::fs::write replaces an existing path. Two live materializations of the same input in one process therefore share a file, so one can overwrite or remove the file still used by the other; a pre-existing same-name path is also overwritten.

Duplicate migration inputs are detected only by lexical PathBuf equality. Aliases such as "file.fsl" and "./file.fsl", or distinct hard links, bypass the check and let the atomic writer process the same destination twice, defeating the stated duplicate-path protection and potentially breaking hard-link identity.
